claim: Perturbation-based and jailbreak-based adversarial attacks targeting verbal confidence scores can significantly impair verbal confidence estimates and induce frequent answer changes.
stance_target: verbal confidence is not just miscalibrated on average but adversarially brittle
scope_conditions: multiple prompting strategies, model sizes, and application domains; published NeurIPS 2025
quoted_support: these attacks can significantly impair verbal confidence estimates and lead to frequent answer changes.

claim: Commonly used defense techniques against verbal-confidence attacks are largely ineffective or counterproductive.
stance_target: existing mitigation strategies can adequately shore up verbal confidence reliability
scope_conditions: evaluated across defense techniques, prompting strategies, model sizes, and domains
quoted_support: current verbal confidence is vulnerable and that commonly used defence techniques are largely ineffective or counterproductive.

claim: Subtle, semantic-preserving modifications to input prompts can lead to misleading verbal confidence outputs without changing the underlying task semantics.
stance_target: verbal confidence robustness fails even under minimal, meaning-preserving perturbation, a distinct failure mode from calibration miscalibration
quoted_support: even subtle semantic-preserving modifications can lead to misleading confidence in responses.
